lessons.name: THE ORDER STRUCTURE AT MODULUS 21. The 12 residues coprime to 21 are all killed by the exponent 6 — a^6 = 1 for every unit a — and no proper divisor of 6 kills them all (all 3 of them checked). So 6 is the exponent of (Z/21)*, the Carmichael lambda, computed here rather than looked up. This is the number every obstruction at this modulus actually turns on: an exponent n reaches the group only through gcd(n, 6), which is why the survey below is indexed by that and not by n.

lessons.name: AN OBSTRUCTION AT MODULUS 42, REDUCED EXPONENT 1. So x^n + y^n = z^n has NO solution in integers with x, y, z all coprime to 42, for EVERY exponent n reducing to 1 — that is n in [5,7,11,13,17,19,23] of the range walked, and every larger n with the same gcd against 6. An unbounded conclusion from a finite table. It settles the coprime case only — classically Case I — and infinitely many triples sharing a factor with 42 pass through untouched, so the coprime half is what it decides and the other half is untouched.
